= Statement of Work: Flox Runtime & Nix Build Integration
:author: AI Assistant + Human Collaborator
:revdate: 2026-02-08
:toc: left
:toclevels: 3
:icons: font

== Context

We are integrating Flox environment management and Nix package builds into the RKE2Lab Kubernetes cluster. Recent work includes:

* Fixed rke2-server restart loop (cilium-operator-scaling script naming)
* Evolved from systemd service approach to Kubernetes-native DaemonSet initContainer
* Implemented nix-builder initContainer using nsenter to access host environment
* Established Flox authentication sharing from Darwin host to cluster nodes via mount
* Created descriptor-driven Nix build system (nix-builds.yaml)

The architecture now follows Kubernetes-native patterns with DaemonSet initContainers running on nodes labeled `flox.dev/enabled=true`.

== Objectives

. Validate DaemonSet initContainer Nix builds in actual deployment
. Verify builds execute successfully on all flox-enabled nodes
. Test multi-node distribution and build caching
. Document Flox runtime architecture and operational procedures
. Establish patterns for Flox-based workloads
. Ensure build observability via kubectl logs

== Scope

=== In Scope

* DaemonSet initContainer nix-builder validation and testing
* Nix build descriptor format and job execution
* Flox environment activation and authentication
* Build output verification and caching strategy
* Kubernetes-native observability (pod logs, events)
* Documentation of architecture decisions and patterns
* Node labeling strategy for Flox enablement

=== Out of Scope

* Flox installation on nodes (pre-installed on host, accessed via nsenter)
* Non-Flox container runtime configurations
* Upstream RKE2 manifests not related to Flox runtime
* Network layer mesh packages usage (separate workload phase)
* Performance optimization (initial focus on correctness)

== Assumptions

* Flox is pre-installed and authenticated on the host
* Nodes have access to host Nix store at /nix
* Flox config mounted from Darwin host at /root/.config/flox
* Scripts bind-mounted from working tree at /srv/host/scripts.d
* nix-builds.yaml descriptor mounted at /srv/host/nix-builds.yaml
* nsenter can access host PID 1 namespace from privileged container
* Node labeling with `flox.dev/enabled=true` controls deployment

== Approach

=== Phase 1: Deployment Validation

.*Objectives*
* Deploy DaemonSet to cluster with nix-builder initContainer
* Verify initContainer starts and runs to completion
* Validate nsenter successfully accesses host environment
* Check Flox activation and Nix store access

.*Tasks*
. Apply DaemonSet manifest to cluster
. Watch pod lifecycle: `kubectl get pods -n flox-runtime -w`
. Check initContainer logs: `kubectl logs -n flox-runtime -l app.kubernetes.io/name=flox-runtime-installer -c nix-builder`
. Verify initContainer completes successfully (exit 0)
. Check for error messages or missing dependencies

.*Acceptance Criteria*
* [x] DaemonSet creates pods on nodes with `flox.dev/enabled=true`
* [x] nix-builder initContainer starts before shim-installer
* [x] nsenter successfully enters host namespace
* [x] Script locates nix-builds.yaml descriptor
* [x] Flox activation succeeds
* [x] No errors in initContainer logs

=== Phase 2: Build Execution Verification

.*Objectives*
* Validate Nix builds execute for all jobs in descriptor
* Verify build outputs are created in expected locations
* Check build logs for errors or warnings
* Confirm builds leverage Nix store and caching

.*Tasks*
. Exec into node to check build outputs: `/tmp/mesh-build`
. Verify binaries built: headplane, headplane-agent, headscale
. Check Nix store for build artifacts
. Review build timing and caching behavior
. Test descriptor with disabled job (enabled: false)
. Test graceful skip when nix-builds.yaml missing

.*Acceptance Criteria*
* [x] All enabled jobs in nix-builds.yaml execute
* [x] Build outputs created in /tmp/{job-name}-build directories
* [x] Binaries are executable and correct architecture
* [x] Disabled jobs are skipped
* [x] Missing descriptor handled gracefully (no failure)
* [x] Build logs show Nix store hits for cached packages

=== Phase 3: Multi-Node Distribution

.*Objectives*
* Validate builds distribute to all flox-enabled nodes
* Test node join/leave behavior
* Verify build consistency across nodes

.*Tasks*
. Label additional nodes with `flox.dev/enabled=true`
. Watch DaemonSet schedule pods on new nodes
. Verify builds execute on newly joined nodes
. Remove label from node, verify pod termination
. Check build artifact presence across all nodes
. Compare build outputs for consistency

.*Acceptance Criteria*
* [x] DaemonSet schedules pods on all labeled nodes
* [x] New nodes execute builds on first startup
* [x] Build artifacts consistent across nodes
* [x] Unlabeling node removes pod gracefully
* [x] Re-labeling triggers fresh deployment

=== Phase 4: Documentation & Patterns

.*Objectives*
* Document Flox runtime architecture
* Create operational runbooks
* Establish reusable patterns for Flox workloads
* Document troubleshooting procedures

.*Tasks*
. Write architecture document: Flox DaemonSet pattern
. Document nix-builds.yaml descriptor format
. Create debugging guide with kubectl commands
. Document nsenter pattern for host environment access
. Establish Flox authentication mount pattern
. Create examples for additional Flox workloads

.*Acceptance Criteria*
* [x] Architecture document in rke2lab/docs/
* [x] Descriptor format specification
* [x] Operational runbook with common operations
* [x] Troubleshooting guide with kubectl commands
* [x] Pattern examples for reuse

== Remote Execution Pattern

Use this command pattern to interact with the cluster and nodes:

[source,bash]
----
# On NixOS VM, orchestrate with remake
ssh bioskop-nixos.local -- flox activate --dir=/var/lib/git/nxmatic/rke2lab -- remake <target>

# Inside Incus node, use flox-activated kubectl
ssh bioskop-nixos.local -- incus exec master -- flox activate --dir=/var/lib/rancher/rke2 -- kubectl <cmd>

# Check DaemonSet status
ssh bioskop-nixos.local -- incus exec master -- flox activate --dir=/var/lib/rancher/rke2 -- kubectl get daemonset -n flox-runtime

# Watch pods
ssh bioskop-nixos.local -- incus exec master -- flox activate --dir=/var/lib/rancher/rke2 -- kubectl get pods -n flox-runtime -w

# View initContainer logs
ssh bioskop-nixos.local -- incus exec master -- flox activate --dir=/var/lib/rancher/rke2 -- kubectl logs -n flox-runtime -l app.kubernetes.io/name=flox-runtime-installer -c nix-builder

# Exec into node to check builds
ssh bioskop-nixos.local -- incus exec master -- ls -la /tmp/mesh-build/
----

== Key Architecture Decisions

.*DaemonSet InitContainer vs Systemd Service*
* *Decision*: Use Kubernetes DaemonSet initContainer
* *Rationale*: 
** Kubernetes-native distribution to all labeled nodes
** Better observability via kubectl logs vs journalctl
** Automatic execution on node join
** Consistent with manifest-based deployment architecture
* *Trade-offs*: Requires privileged container for nsenter access

.*nsenter to Host vs Container Tools*
* *Decision*: Use nsenter to run script in host namespace
* *Rationale*:
** Avoids installing flox/nix/yq in container
** Direct access to host's Nix store and Flox config
** Simpler volume mount strategy
** Leverages pre-installed host environment
* *Trade-offs*: Requires privileged container, tightly coupled to host

.*Nix Builds in InitContainer vs Main Container*
* *Decision*: Run builds in initContainer before shim installation
* *Rationale*:
** Builds available before containerd shim needs them
** Failed builds don't block shim (graceful degradation)
** Clear lifecycle: build → install → run
* *Trade-offs*: Builds block pod startup (acceptable for node setup)
